description: Poly Unison: turns each channel of a polyphonic pitch input into a detuned unison spread and merges the result into one polyphonic output

params.text: Sets how many unison voices each input channel becomes, from 1 to 16
Sets the spread the unison voices are detuned across, measured in semitones and divided evenly between them; with a count of 1 it changes nothing
Sets where the spread falls around the input pitch: grey divides it evenly above and below, green runs from the input pitch upwards, red runs from below and ends at the input pitch
Sets how far the DETUNE knob reaches: grey 1 semitone, blue 1 octave, green 5 octaves
Sets the channel order at the output: yellow keeps all the voices of one input channel together, blue lays out the input channels as a set and repeats the whole set

inputs.text: Monophonic bipolar CV added to the COUNT knob, a third of a volt for each voice, the total clamped between 1 and 16
Monophonic bipolar CV added to the DETUNE knob, 10V covering the whole range that knob has; a menu option reads this input at a volt per octave instead
The polyphonic pitch whose channels become unison spreads; unpatched it counts as one channel of 0V. A lamp glows yellow for each channel that could be replicated and red for each that could not

outputs.text: Every unison voice merged into one polyphonic cable, each group running from the lowest voice of the spread to the highest

menu: Add Auxilliary Clone expander — places one immediately to the right, giving four more polyphonic input and output pairs replicated by the same count, though those copies carry no detuning
V/Oct Detune CV — reads the DETUNE CV input at a volt per octave instead of 10V covering the whole range of the knob
